findings.claim: MemCompiler supplies the strongest science-domain same-memory delivery ablation found so far: Qwen-2.5-14B ScienceWorld Full state-conditioned compilation is 46.67 completion / 69.33 partial score, while AMMI static injection of the same retrieved M is 27.93 / 52.68. The paper explicitly frames this row as isolating dynamic compilation.
findings.scope: Same fixed retrieved candidate pool M; not exact per-step selected-item identity fixed, and not a pure accept/reject-bit-only manipulation.

findings.claim: At current official revision ec5a579..., the ScienceWorld runner retrieves successful task(s)/insights once before the episode loop using task_text and then reuses the same task_memory object while the Manager receives current observation, score, working memory and history each step. Per-step state conditioning is therefore a Manager compilation/guidance layer over a fixed episode-level candidate pool, not repeated bank retrieval.
findings.scope: Current public code only; evaluated revision binding remains unresolved.

findings.claim: The same public ScienceWorld runner logs Manager inputs/outputs and only task_memory_summary counts in the final detailed trajectory, not stable candidate-member IDs/digests or a machine-readable per-step selected-memory identity. Thus exact per-item fixed-retrieval counterfactual replay is not recoverable from this public trace without instrumentation.
findings.scope: Public trace observability only; no claim about private author logs.

findings.claim: The official MemCompiler project page links a 44.8 GB Hugging Face learned-model artifact with two public commits on 2026-05-29, partially resolving the search for external artifacts. It has no model card and does not publicly bind itself to a Table-3 run, exact code revision, memory-bank snapshot or candidate-pool digest.
findings.scope: Learned model exists; evaluated memory/data identity remains unresolved.

findings.claim: CaSKG (2026-08-26) reports a six-backbone macro ScienceWorld improvement from 72.62 (GoS) to 80.50 using an offline counterfactual-calibrated, state-filtered skill graph while leaving the downstream policy/task interface unchanged.
findings.scope: Retrieval-structure intervention, not fixed selected-candidate receiver acceptance.

findings.claim: CaSKG's paper says code is available at its advertised GitHub repository, but exact public main revision 39430e73015ab2f13f55ed7c59c141e452c40ba3 contains only README.md saying code will be released within a few days. The advertised public repo is therefore not yet replay-ready for the reported ScienceWorld result.
findings.scope: Exact advertised GitHub surface only; alternate/private artifacts not excluded.

findings.claim: SAMem reports GPT-4o ScienceWorld average reward 65.4 versus CDMem 52.1 and no-memory 35.5 over an unseen 90-task ScienceWorld evaluation covering all 30 task types.
findings.scope: Cross-method state-aware memory support, not isolated receiver gate.

findings.claim: SAMem's GPT-4o component ablation drops ScienceWorld average reward from 65.4 full to 47.4 without Q-learning and 48.5 without situation processing, confirming state representation/value-aware memory as load-bearing but not holding memory/retrieved identity fixed.
findings.scope: Do not treat as fixed-bank/fixed-selected-identity acceptance-only causality.

protocols.name: MEMORY_SELECTION_TRACE_BINDING
protocols.rule: Distinguish a fixed-candidate-pool state-conditioned claim from a stronger fixed-selected-identity receiver-acceptance claim. The stronger claim requires frozen memory, exact bank/pool/state/selector bindings, available per-condition selection traces with identical selected IDs+digests, identical compiled-guidance digest, and an inject-versus-abstain contrast as the sole declared manipulated variable. If selection is implicit/unlogged, the weaker fixed-candidate-pool claim remains legal but must not be elevated.
protocols.test_result: 8/8 expected semantic outcomes; 8/8 cases structurally valid under Draft 2020-12.
